test.title: Magnetic Effects of Current - Test 7
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: A circular loop of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is carrying current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>. The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of circular loop and at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> from the center of the loop on its axis is :

A proton, a deuteron and an <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>-particle with same kinetic energy enter into a uniform magnetic field at right angle to magnetic field. The ratio of the radii of their respective circular paths is :
Find the magnetic field at point P due to a straight line segment AB of length 6 cm carrying a current of 5 A. (See figure) μ0=4π×10-7 NA-2

A beam of protons with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> enters a uniform magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> to the magnetic field, the pitch of the resulting helical path of protons is close to : (Mass of the proton<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>67</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, charge of the proton<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>69</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>)
A hairpin like shape as shown in figure is made by bending a long current carrying wire. What is the magnitude of a magnetic field at point P which lies on the centre of the semicircle ?

An electron, moving along the x- axis with an initial energy of 100 eV, enters a region of magnetic field B→=1.5×10-3 Tk^ at S (see figure). The field extends between x=0 and x=2 cm. The electron is detected at the point Q on a screen placed 8 cm away from the point S. The distance d between P and Q (on the screen) is:
(electron’s charge 1.6×10-19 C , mass of electron =9.1×10-31 kg )

Two long current carrying conductors are placed parallel to each other at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> between them. The magnitude of magnetic field produced at mid-point between the two conductors due to current flowing in them is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μT</mi></math>. The equal current flowing in the two conductors is :

Radiation, with wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6561</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Å</mi></math> falls on a metal surface to produce photoelectrons. The electrons are made to enter a uniform magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> . If the radius of the largest circular path followed by the electrons is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> , the work function of the metal is close to:

A particle having the same charge as of electron moves in a circular path of radius 0.5 cm under the influence of a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If an electric field of 100 V/m makes it to move in a straight path, then the mass of the particle is (Given charge of electron =1.6×10-19C )

A current of 1.5 A is flowing through a triangle, of side 9 cm each. The magnetic field at the centroid of the triangle is :
(Assume that the current is flowing in the clockwise direction.)

A particle of charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> and mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is moving with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mi>v</mi><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> towards a large screen placed in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>Z</mi></math> plane at distance d. If there is magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></math> the minimum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> for which the particle will not hit the screen is :

The ratio of B2B1 is:

The magnetic field at a point along the axis at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> from the centre is :

A wire A, bent in the shape of an arc of a circle, carrying a current of 2 A and having radius 2 cm and another wire B, also bent in the shape of an arc of a circle, carrying a current of 3 A and having radius of 4 cm, are placed as shown in the figure. The ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wires A and B at the common centre O is:

The electric current in a circular coil of four turns produces a magnetic induction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>32</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> at its centre. The coil is unwound and is rewound into a circular coil of single turn, the magnetic induction at the centre of the coil by the same current will be :

A thin ring of <math><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> radius carries a uniformly distributed charge. The ring rotates at a constant angular speed of <math><mn>40</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> about its axis, perpendicular to its plane. Is the magnetic field its centre is <math><mn>3.8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> , then the charge carried by the ring is close to <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>

The magnetic field at the center of current carrying circular loop is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. The magnetic field at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math> times radius of the given circular loop from the center on its axis is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> will be

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></math> are the magnetic field at the centre of two coils of two coils <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> respectively, each carrying equal current. If coil <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn></math> turns and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> radius and coil <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn></math> turns and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> radius, the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></math> is

Two <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> long, straight wires, each carrying a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> are kept parallel to each other. If each wire experienced a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, then separation between the wires is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

The magnetic field at the centre of a wire loop formed by two semicircular wires of radii R1=2π m and R2=4π m carrying current I=4 A as per figure given below is α×10-7 T. The value of α is _____. (Centre O is common for all segments)

A charge particle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μC</mi></math> accelerated by a potential difference of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> enters a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mT</mi></math> at right angle to the direction of field. The charge particle completes semicircle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> inside magnetic field. The mass of the charge particle is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>.

A tightly wound long solenoid carries a current of 1.5 A . An electron is executing uniform circular motion inside the solenoid with a time period of 75 ns . The number of turns per metre in the solenoid is $\ldots\ldots$ -.
[Take mass of electron $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$, charge of electron $\left|\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{e}}\right|=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$,
$\left.\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \frac{\mathrm{~N}}{\mathrm{~A}^2}, 1 \mathrm{~ns}=10^{-9} \mathrm{~s}\right]$

The current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> flows in a square loop of sides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is placed in air. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> is _________.
